question: The 2025 Eurovision Song Contest took place in Basel, Switzerland, yet the 2026 contest was staged in Vienna, Austria. Why did Austria get to host it?
correct_answer: Austria won Eurovision 2025, winner hosts next
alternative_answers: The winning country hosts the following year
headline_answer: Austria won Eurovision 2025, winner hosts next
source_excerpt: Vienna was picked in August 2025, beating Innsbruck.

extra.verification_notes: Austria (JJ, 'Wasted Love') won Eurovision 2025 in Basel, so Vienna hosted 2026 under the winner-hosts convention; see https://www.euronews.com/culture/2025/08/20/eurovision-song-contest-2026-to-take-place-in-vienna

explanation: Eurovision is traditionally hosted by the country that won the previous year. Austrian singer JJ won the 2025 contest in Basel with the song Wasted Love, so Austria earned the right to stage the 2026 edition and chose Vienna, which had already hosted in 1967 and 2015. The same rule explains why Basel hosted in 2025: Switzerland's Nemo had won in Malmo in 2024. Following that rule again, Bulgaria, which won in Vienna in 2026 with Dara's Bangaranga, is set to host in 2027.

question: In February 2026, which artist won Album of the Year at the Grammys and then, exactly one week later, headlined the Super Bowl halftime show?
source_excerpt: Bad Bunny won the 2026 Grammy Album of the Year for Debí Tirar Más Fotos.

extra.why_interesting: Players know both events separately; realising one artist did both within seven days, in Spanish, is the delight.
extra.verification_notes: Bad Bunny won Album of the Year on Feb 1, 2026 and headlined Super Bowl LX halftime on Feb 8, 2026, exactly one week later (https://www.complex.com/music/a/tracewilliamcowen/2026-grammys-winners).

explanation: His album Debí Tirar Más Fotos was the first Spanish-language record ever to take Album of the Year, and his halftime show in Santa Clara was performed almost entirely in Spanish.

question: Kendrick Lamar and SZA's Record of the Year winner at the 2026 Grammys takes its title from the first name of which soul singer, whose 1982 duet is sampled throughout the track?
source_excerpt: Kendrick Lamar With SZA won the 2026 Grammy Award for Record Of The Year with "luther".

extra.why_interesting: Many players have heard the lowercase title without ever asking who 'luther' is; the answer connects a 2026 winner to a 1980s soul legend.
extra.verification_notes: "luther" by Kendrick Lamar & SZA won 2026 Record of the Year and samples Luther Vandross & Cheryl Lynn's 1982 'If This World Were Mine'; see https://luthervandross.com/luther-wins-record-of-the-year-at-the-2026-grammys/

explanation: The song is built on Vandross and Cheryl Lynn's version of 'If This World Were Mine', and it gave Kendrick Lamar back-to-back Record of the Year wins after 'Not Like Us' in 2025.

question: Which comedian hosted the Grammy Awards in 2026 for the sixth consecutive year?
source_excerpt: Trevor Noah to Host Grammys for 6th and Final Time

extra.why_interesting: Players expect the Grammys to rotate hosts like the Oscars; a six-year streak by one comedian is the surprise.
extra.verification_notes: Trevor Noah hosted the 2026 Grammys, his sixth consecutive time (2021-2026) and billed as his last, per https://cms.grammy.com/news/2026-grammys-trevor-noah-host-announcement/.

explanation: The former Daily Show host has fronted every Grammy ceremony since 2021, a run no modern Grammys host has matched.

question: After Austria's victory at the 2025 contest, which city hosted the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest?
source_excerpt: The 2026 contest was held at the Wiener Stadthalle in Vienna, Austria. The semi-finals were on 12 and 14 May 2026, and the final was on 16 May 2026.

extra.why_interesting: The player only needs to remember who won in 2025 and reason to the capital; the payoff is that Vienna had already hosted a decade earlier thanks to Conchita Wurst.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms the 2026 contest was held at the Wiener Stadthalle in Vienna after Austria's 2025 win: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2026

explanation: It was Vienna's second time as host, following 2015, when Conchita Wurst's win the year before brought the contest to the same Wiener Stadthalle.

question: The 2026 Brit Awards were staged outside London for the first time in the ceremony's history. Which city hosted them?
source_excerpt: The ceremony took place on 28 February 2026 at Co-op Live in Manchester, the first time the ceremony was held outside London.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume the Brits are permanently a London event; the move north to the city of Oasis, Joy Division and The Smiths is a neat twist.
extra.verification_notes: The 2026 Brit Awards were held at Co-op Live, Manchester, the first ceremony outside London, per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Awards_2026.

explanation: The ceremony moved to the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, fitting for a city that gave Britain Oasis, Joy Division and The Smiths.

question: In October 2025, Taylor Swift's The Life of a Showgirl set a new record for the biggest sales week ever in the United States. Whose album 25, released in 2015, held the record before her?
source_excerpt: 4.002 million equivalent album units, comprising 3.479 million traditional album sales... beats 25's 3.482 million equivalent album units (or 3.378 million traditional album sales) in its first week.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume the previous record was another Swift album; the real holder was a ten-year-old Adele record, which gives a satisfying 'of course' moment.
extra.verification_notes: Showgirl's 4.002M first-week units beat Adele's 25 (3.482M units, 3.378M pure sales), and no 2026 release has come close (https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/780151-fastest-selling-album-in-the-us).

explanation: Swift moved roughly four million units in seven days, overtaking the mark Adele's 25 had held for a full decade.

question: Which singer, who had opened for Taylor Swift on the Eras Tour, is the only guest vocalist on The Life of a Showgirl, duetting on its 2025 title track?
source_excerpt: Sabrina Carpenter appears on the title track, 'The Life of a Showgirl.'

extra.why_interesting: The album's only guest is the opening act who became a superstar during that same tour; the foothold lets a casual fan reason their way there.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms Sabrina Carpenter, an Eras Tour opener, duets on the title track and lists no other guest vocalists, but I read only part of the page and did not search for newer events.

explanation: Carpenter warmed up Eras Tour crowds in 2023 and 2024, then closed Swift's twelfth album as its sole featured artist.

question: Which Netflix animated film produced 'Golden', the song by a fictional girl group that won Best Original Song at the 2026 Oscars?
source_excerpt: HUNTR/X's Golden makes Oscars history becoming first KPop track to win for Best Original Song

extra.why_interesting: A song by a cartoon girl group beat every live-action contender; the player who watched the film with their kids gets an easy win.
extra.verification_notes: Golden from Netflix's KPop Demon Hunters won Best Original Song at the 98th Oscars (March 2026), per https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/huntrx-golden-oscar-winner-2026-ejae-speech

explanation: The track, sung by the demon-fighting trio HUNTR/X, became the first K-pop song to win an Oscar and had already spent eight weeks at number one on the US Hot 100 in 2025.

question: Oasis's 2025 reunion tour was the band's first run of concerts since the Gallagher brothers fell out and split. In which year had Oasis broken up?

extra.why_interesting: Everyone knows the reunion was 'long overdue' but few can place the split; the sixteen-year gap feels longer or shorter than people expect.
extra.verification_notes: Oasis split on 28 August 2009 when Noel Gallagher quit before the Rock en Seine show in Paris (https://news.pollstar.com/2009/08/31/noel-gallagher-quits-oasis/); no newer event contradicts this.

explanation: The band ended backstage at a Paris festival in August 2009, so the Cardiff opening night in July 2025 came almost sixteen years later.

question: BTS's March 2026 comeback album, their first as a full group after the members finished military service, shares its name with which traditional Korean folk song?
source_excerpt: Arirang is the tenth overall studio album by BTS, released on March 20, 2026, through BigHit Music.

extra.why_interesting: The biggest comeback in K-pop history was named after Korea's best-known folk song; a player who knows one Korean song can reason to it.
extra.verification_notes: BTS's March 20, 2026 album 'Arirang' is named after the traditional Korean folk song, per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arirang_(album); nothing newer contradicts this.

explanation: The album debuted at number one in the US alongside its single 'Swim', and the title nods to the folk song often called Korea's unofficial anthem.

question: Which British soul singer won Best New Artist at the 2026 Grammys and, a few weeks later, both Artist of the Year and Album of the Year at the 2026 Brit Awards for her album The Art of Loving?
source_excerpt: Olivia Dean – The Art Of Loving

extra.why_interesting: Players expect a Best New Artist Grammy to go to an American pop act; in 2026 it went to a London soul singer who, within weeks, also swept the top prizes at her home country's Brit Awards for her album The Art of Loving.
extra.verification_notes: Dean won Grammy Best New Artist (1 Feb 2026) and Brit Awards Artist and Album of the Year for The Art of Loving (28 Feb 2026); no contradicting developments found.

explanation: Dean's second album The Art of Loving turned her from a UK favourite into a transatlantic winner, taking the Grammy for Best New Artist in February 2026 and then the Brits' two biggest awards.
